meta.title: Rapid Biofabrication of an Advanced Microphysiological System Mimicking Phenotypical Heterogeneity and Drug Resistance in Glioblastoma.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A hydrogel microphysiological system with a brain-endothelial vessel channel was rapidly printed to co-culture glioblastoma cells and astrocytes, avoiding PDMS so drug tests aren't skewed. It reproduced two GBM cell populations and drug resistance.

formulations.review_notes: Viability is a threshold ('above 80%'). Which parts were printed vs cast should be checked.
formulations.name: Fibrin gel (4 mg/mL) in printed microfluidic hydrogel
formulations.cell_type: U87 glioblastoma cells, astrocytes, brain endothelial cells
formulations.key_outcome: All cell types stayed above 80% viable; the model showed GBM heterogeneity and drug resistance.

evidence.quote: were used at the final concentration of 4 mg mL−1 and 1 U mL−1, respectively to obtain fibrin gel
All the cell types maintain cell viability above 80% while cultured on the 3D‐bioprinted model.
